authorization: User explicitly requested further improvement iteration after the failed memory study. This is a new study; the old gate and conclusions remain unchanged.
hypothesis: Combine ammo-change and previous-hit feedback so a one-window rest still detects a firing event when ammo replenishment hides consumption. Both signals must be observed before the current decision.

selection.rank: One fixed candidate, combined_rest1. Require development utility and kill criteria against rules in both scenarios. No search or fallback to an ablation.

confirmation_arms: Fixed combined-event candidate, original rules, ammo-only and hit-only ablations, command_rest1, and all five preserved history_MAP fits. Same seeds, steering, horizon and action cost; randomized single-worker order.
primary: Selected minus rules and selected minus the mean of the five preserved history_MAP fits in each of two scenarios.

confirmation_gate.interval: 99.375% two-sided paired percentile bootstrap, Bonferroni for four utility and four kill comparisons. Resample seeds and history training fits. Exploratory finite-sample evidence, not guaranteed coverage.

secondary: Matched no-rest and command-rest controls identify simpler explanations; kills, ammo used, actual engine reward, truncations, success and firing windows, total decision compute.
claim_boundary: Handwritten event-memory control, not Bayesian RL, new architecture or adaptive computation. Both scenarios are used in development. Confirmation seeds are fresh but this is not unseen-task generalization. Historical memory rules traces motivated the two signals before new confirmation. Command-window utility may reward suppressing commands; require kill noninferiority and report engine metrics. No per-shot accuracy, second-environment or ICLR novelty claim.
design_evidence: evidence/cadence-doom-v1/historical-diagnostic.json plus prior published ammo-replenishment limitation; the ongoing ammo-only confirmation does not select parameters of this fixed candidate.
